clue.text: Room with sign portraying astronauts

parts.note: room in the sense of free space
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A room bearing a sign that depicts astronauts.
explanation.definitionFit: Female space travellers are astronauts, plural like the definition.

clue.text: George almost paid out a penny less for small 22 down of 15?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are jumbled into a new order
almost means the last letter of the name is dropped
less means the following item is taken away from the word paid

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for an old British penny (denarius)

explanation.surface: George was paid a penny short for a small bit of a piano composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims George to GEORG; 'less' takes D (old penny) from PAID, leaving PAI; 'out' scrambles GEORGPAI. 22 down is PART, 15 is PIANO PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord played note by note is a small part of many piano pieces.

clue.text: Those with head branches spread around six counties? I'd say not

indicators.note: the antlered beasts are spread around the other piece, which sits inside them

parts.note: deer carry antlers, branches on their heads
Northern Ireland is made up of six counties

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about antlered animals roaming over Ulster, met with a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is the usual short form for Northern Ireland, whose six counties are the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who denies things might say these words, so the phrase stands for that person.

clue.text: Film about unknown 15s

indicators.note: about means the film title goes round the other piece

parts.note: Kes is a 1969 British film about a boy and his kestrel
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A film concerning some unidentified piano pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The individual levers of a piano keyboard can loosely be called parts or pieces of a piano.

clue.text: Like some stamps fellow in post office valued without hesitation

indicators.note: in places the hesitation and fellow inside the post office

parts.note: er is the sound of a hesitation
valued means rated, assessed for worth

explanation.surface: A man at the post office priced some stamps promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' misleads as 'promptly', but ER (hesitation) goes with F into PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets of stamps are punched with rows of small holes so they tear apart easily.

clue.text: Religious picture explosive turned up in city lake

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: in puts the reversed explosive inside the lake

parts.note: Como is a lake in northern Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A devotional painting is blown upward by a bomb in a lakeside city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suits a down clue, where the reversed piece reads upward; EC is the City of London's postcode, and 'in' sets the turned explosive inside the Italian lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce Homo ('Behold the man') is a painting subject showing Christ crowned with thorns.

clue.text: 15's beat

definitions.meaning: a piano's action includes felt-covered strikers that hit the strings
to beat is to strike repeatedly

explanation.definitionFit: A piano has felt-tipped strikers, and to strike blows is to beat.

clue.text: Relative has half of 15 daughter lost

indicators.note: lost means the daughter's letter is removed

parts.note: the first half of 15 is piano, and a grand is a kind of piano

explanation.surface: A relative owns a piano now that her daughter has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother, familiarly gran, is a family relative.

clue.text: Theatre turns hard to endure? Don't give up

indicators.note: turns means the word for theatre is read backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
something severe is hard to bear

explanation.surface: Encouragement to stick with a gruelling stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going in spite of difficulty is the same as not giving up.

clue.text: I recall nude playing 15

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performed in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls performing in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Debussy's Clair de Lune is a famous solo piano composition.

clue.text: Directs different ending to film

indicators.note: different asks for the letters in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A director chooses another finale for a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of cast and crew rolls at the close of a movie.

clue.text: Citizen especially honoured following return of title by monarch

indicators.note: return of means the title and monarch together are read backwards

parts.note: a title is a name
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A citizen gains honour when a sovereign restores a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given the freedom of a city is a citizen granted a special honour.

clue.text: Bet widow's missing do

indicators.note: missing means the party word is taken out of the widow

parts.note: a dowager is a widow holding her late husband's title
a do is a party, here simply the letters

explanation.surface: A bet that the widow will miss the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a bet, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Rugby player on tour, drunk when about to start boarding plane

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the other piece
drunk suggests the letters reel into a new order
to start points to the first letter of boarding

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: A rugby player on tour gets drunk just before boarding the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles the tour letters and 'about' wraps them round the first letter of boarding ('to start'); 'on' just places the rugby forward after that.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a plane driven by a propeller turned by a gas turbine.

clue.text: You'll see her setting off to find things to help provide closure

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are set off into a new order

explanation.surface: You'll watch her leaving to look for something that brings closure.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that tighten things help close them firmly.

clue.text: Something scored by Ian, perhaps?

parts.note: read one way, a musical work for the keyboard; read another, the name Ian is itself a run of letters inside the instrument's name

explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard composition is something scored, and Ian is literally a fragment of the instrument's name.

clue.text: Doctor has gin — not a lot — after second 15

indicators.note: after says the doctored letters come behind the word for a second

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a small gin a moment later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the physician but is the anagram signal; the dashes make 'not a lot' look like an aside about the gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata is a celebrated work for solo piano.

clue.text: Sticky sweet bound to have one 23 down centre? Not exactly

indicators.note: to have means the leap word holds the other letters

parts.note: to lollop is to bound along clumsily
I is the Roman numeral one
23 down is soft, and P (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: A sticky sweet is certain to have a soft middle, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre? Not exactly' notes that IP goes in LOLLOP slightly off the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Sailor girl's beginning to look strange

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
Norma is a girl's name

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter of look

explanation.surface: A sailor's girlfriend is starting to look odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means unusual or out of the ordinary, as strange does.

clue.text: Lumpy custard finally eaten by one adult's revolting

indicators.note: eaten by means the custard's letter is swallowed inside the others
revolting means the letters rise up into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of custard

explanation.surface: Lumpy custard, swallowed by a grown-up, is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' makes NOULATED from ONE ADULT; 'eaten by' puts D (from 'custard finally') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulated means covered in small knobs or nodules, which is lumpy.

clue.text: See 10
Breeding of a little dog

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small dog showing a hint of good breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is a wild dog of Australia.

clue.text: Agent crazy about 15

indicators.note: about means the agent and crazy pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: An agent goes wild over a piece of piano music.
explanation.definitionFit: A damper is the felt pad that silences a piano string, a piece of the instrument.

clue.text: Parking topless large figure in extra seat

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a million is a large number

explanation.surface: A topless figure takes a spare seat in the car park.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is the passenger seat behind a motorcycle rider.

clue.text: Catch up with second half of 15

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to trap is to catch

explanation.surface: Catch up with the rest of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second half of 15 is piece, and a piece is a part.

clue.text: US army nearly stunned first-rate swordsman

indicators.note: stunned suggests the letters are knocked into a new order
nearly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

explanation.surface: American soldiers were nearly floored by a superb swordsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims US ARMY to USARM; 'stunned' rearranges it as SAMUR. A1 is taken as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a Japanese warrior famed for swordsmanship.

clue.text: Drunkard hugs female giving first half of 15

indicators.note: hugs means the drunkard wraps around the other letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk embraces a woman, giving the first half of a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the Italian musical term for soft.

clue.text: 22 down of 15, say, providing boy with tonic

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name
do (doh) is the tonic note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A piano part, perhaps, for a boy with a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo, with its returning theme, is an example of a piece for piano.

clue.text: Curved neural pathway in cord in bottom bit of cortex

indicators.note: in places the cord inside the bottom

parts.note: rear means bottom
flex is electrical cord

indicators.note: bit of picks the first letter of cortex

explanation.surface: A curved nerve route through the cord ends at the lower cortex.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex arc is the route a nerve impulse follows to trigger a reflex.
